personnages.premiere: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy (2001)
personnages.jeux_phares: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy (2001)

personnages.description: Skully was a member of LeChuck's undead crew during his attack on Plunder Island. His head was knocked off accidentally by LeChuck while he was calling out over the battlefield to Elaine Marley. With his head on the deck, he was able to spot Guybrush Threepwood floating towards The Death Starfish on board a bumper car.

Kenny Falmouth is a juvenile entrepreneur based in Puerto Pollo, the main town of Plunder Island. He was notorious for selling lemonade with a special bottomless mug policy. When that venture failed, he moved on to selling cannons for pirates and privateers. His ventures were supported by his mother, whom he would often call out.

:"I am Madame Xima... Mistress of the ancient arts of precognition and augury... Diva of divination". Madame Xima is an elderly fortune teller who could be found at the Goodsoup Hotel in Blood Island. While many dismissed her practice, it was clear that she could predict the future with her deck of tarot cards and psychic visions. She claimed to be far beyond that of a normal fortune teller, possibly using similar mystical powers as the Voodoo Lady. She claimed she had the power to "put a curse on you that would make every morsel of food you eat... become a ravenous cockroach inside your intestines... giving you the most excruciating death imaginable". She is the only regular patron at the hotel due to her bizarre and abrasive personality frightening away potential customers. Upon meeting Guybrush Threepwood, Xima foretold his future, foreseeing evil men and an island in the shape of a skull. She used her tarot cards and repeatedly drew 'Death' cards totaling five, which Threepwood then stole from her.

Dinghy Dog is every piratey kid's favorite cartoon character. He was considered the park's most popular character, much to Wharf Rat's discontentment. He seems to be LeChuck's right-hand man and his figure was used as the mascot for the Carnival of the Damned amusement park. He wore a dog costume, and a blue hat with the word 'Dinghy'. He was considered the park's most popular character, much to Wharf Rat's discontentment. He had somewhat of a silly demeanor, though he didn't mind biting back if pressed. He speaks with a hillbilly accent and drawl and would often remark 'Yup!' while speaking. Guybrush finds a stuffed Dinghy Dog toy in the stomach of Man-eating Snake at the Snake X-ing. Obviously it belonged to a victim of that snake. The toy reads "I Whooped It Up At Big Whoop". When Guybrush Threepwood arrives to the Carnival of the Damned, he acts like he already knows Dinghy Dog, as someone very famous, although he isn't referenced before (other than the stuffed toy). It's possible that they had met while he was trapped in Big Whoop. He first appears as one of LeChuck's closest henchmen, and served him during his resurrection as a demon pirate in The Curse of Monkey Island. LeChuck ordered him to find Elaine, who would be somewhere near Guybrush. Later he appears announcing that he and his men had found Guybrush and Elaine Marley somewhere on Blood Island. Later, Dinghy would be seen running a game which had him guessing the customer's weight or age. He also served as the

Captain Blondebeard is the proprietor of Blondebeard's Chicken Shop a chicken restaurant located near the center of Puerto Pollo, the main town of Plunder Island. While a kindly and warm individual, he nevertheless did not take criticism of his cooking lightly. Blondebeard regarded himself a Connoisseur o' Carrion, and claimed to be a huge fan of his fried chicken recipe. One of the things he enjoyed most of his cooking was the crunchiness of the beaks between his teeth. He has been a member of the Brimstone Beach Country Club and Smorgy since 1632, after threatening to run the management all through. He greatly feared the dreaded El Pollo Diablo, otherwise known as "The Demon Chicken", and vowed revenge after his chickens were set free.
Cruff is the right hand man of the notorious smuggler King Andre on Skull Island. He was portrayed as a stereotypically brawny and dim-witted henchman; and left much of the scheming to King Andre.

"If there's any treasure to be found, I'm going to be the man to find it. And I'll look absolutely STUNNING while I'm doing it." Rene Rottingham was a fearsome scoundrel and pirate captain seen in The Curse of Monkey Island. He was a Frenchman and master swordsman and reputed to be the most cunning and well-groomed captain ever to sail the Caribbean. An arrogant man, he was extremely proud of his hair, and would mock anyone with hair he deemed to look bad. He massaged his scalp lovingly with the finest creams and oils in the world, twice daily. He was willing to kill men for insulting his grooming. His self importance had him boast that he would serve under no one elses command. His ship was armed with the Destructomatic T-47 Cannon.

The Flying Welshman is a mysterious ferryman that spent most of his time ferrying people between the islands Blood Island and Skull Island, organizing haunted tours and whale-watching excursions. He was later referred to as the Lost Welshman, after the lighthouse on Blood Island stopped functioning, leaving him trapped in the accursed mists.

The Cabaña Boy was the vendor of the Weenie Hut at the entrance of the Brimstone Beach Country Club and Smorgy on Plunder Island. He was very particular of the country club's exclusivity, and snootily refused to allow anyone without a membership access to the beach, or to partake in any of its amenities, most notably the grill's Cooking Oil and towels.

Slappy Cromwell is the stagename of Rex Fortune, Adventure Seeker, a thespian and playwright. In Curse of Monkey Island, Slappy was busy preparing for his stage production, SPEARE!: A Theatrical Medley, his personal take of classic Shakespearean works,

Griswold Goodsoup is the proud proprietor of the Goodsoup Inn. He was part of long line of restaurateurs that first made name for themselves by establishing a very popular line of soup kitchens in the Caribbean. He played the piano and wrote/composed shows like Highly Explosive!. He admitted to being fabulously wealthy, and enjoyed reminiscing about his ancestry. Despite his societal status, he was a warm and friendly individual, and welcomed guests with open arms. Things took the turn for the worse when Mount Acidophilus, the island's volcano ceased its regular eruptions, because of the Cannibals' rituals. Business dried up, and Griswold fell into a deep depression. He tried everything to sustain the flow of tourists to his inn, but all his efforts were in vain. His only regular guest was Madame Xima who gave everyone the creeps. He soon found himself drinking quite heavily, which led to severe hangover the following day. Guybrush Threepwood created a remedy for him from Pirate Potables. He was delighted when Guybrush caused the volcano to erupt again. He planned to release a dramatic musical he was preparing all this time: Voulez Vous Vichyssoise: the story of a talented young soup chef with revolutionary ideas about soup preparation, cruelly taken down by the Paris culinary establishment.

King André is the self-proclaimed "king of the smugglers", and ruled over his tiny lair on Skull Island. He was bald and spoke with a slight Jamaican accent. Despite his deceitfulness and megalomania, he fancied himself a shrewd businessman, selling a variety of quality merchandise from all over the Carribean, like whole collections of Smuggle Bunnies. He was fond of high stakes card games and relished in his opponents' defeat. He always made sure that the odds were in his favor, as losing was never an option. When LeChuck was still alive, he sold to him the Goodsoup Family Diamond in exchange for a ship; LeChuck had stolen the diamond from Minnie Goodsoup, a debutante that lived on the neighboring Blood Island. It became André's most prized possession, and he claimed that its flowing energy was the source of his power and wealth. He enjoyed having a good laugh that freaked Guybush out, especially when it's at someone's expense. He also had a loyal henchman, Cruff. One of his plans was having rigged Blood Island with explosives controlled by a network of satellites in geosynchronous orbit.

Palido Domingo is an unusually pale-skinned talent manager, and could be found sunbathing in Brimstone Beach Country Club and Smorgy in Plunder Island. He comes off rather rude towards Guybrush, mistaking him for a waiter. His longtime client was thespian and playwright Slappy Cromwell. The two shared a long working relationship back when Cromwell was performing on Blood Island. So long in fact, that Domingo had the map to Blood Island tattooed to his back.

:"Uh oh. I'm hearing the voices again". :-Mr. Fossey Mr. Fossey is the unhinged first mate of Captain LeChimp aboard The Sea Cucumber, which itself had a crew entirely made of monkeys. Mr. Fossey believed he could hear the voice of his captain, despite nobody else being able to. He had habit of hearing his master's call just as he was about to say his name. This meant many assuming he worked for the dreaded pirate LeChuck. Though, after Guybrush infiltrates the ship and discovers that the captain is actually an ape, he realizes that Mr. Fossey is nothing but "an utter loon". He believed that the captain and his crew would use the golden statue of Elaine Marley they stole from the beach to buy an entire fleet of ships and become the ultimate terror of the Caribbean. He was fond of chicken and occasionally ordered from Blondebeard's Chicken Shoppe.

Mort was a gravedigger living in Mort's Shack in the Blood Island Cemetery. He owned a dog called Old Blind Pew. He claimed he was a vegan and was against the exploitation of animals. He was also a horror fan and budding horror novelist, having written the first part of horror trilogy called The Grog that Drank People. He claimed that some crazy kids often made him pranks, talking to him through the crack opening into the Goodsoup Family Crypt.He also was a target of The Voodoo Kids for their Paper Voodoo Dolls. While in the Voodoo 'n' Things, Guybrush pulled a pin from his paper voodoo doll relieving from the pain. He also could (unwittingly believing the doll to be just a toy) torture the gravedigger by using the Pin, the Ember on a Stick, and the Bread Knife, and also scratch his back by using Murray's arm. Later he were telling a joke to Griswold Goodsoup and buried Guybrush in the coffin in the Blood Island Municipal Housing for the Deceased believing him to be dead (though Guybrush was just unconscious from spiking grog with The Head-B-Clear). He does this again later but this time because Guybrush convinced Griswold he was a member of the Goodsoup family, he gets buried in The Goodsoup Crypt instead. When Guybrush talks to him through a crack in the crypt leading to his hut, he refused to believe that Guybrush was locked in the crypt and thought that he is one of the local punks that pranked him, therefore refused to let him out of the crypt. Being into horror novels G
Stu Boyle is the spokesmodel for SPEARE!: A Theatrical Medley. He was also playing Juliet.

The Thin Pirate was an associate of the Fat Pirate (actualy big-boned). After the Battle of Plunder Island, their ship was near Plunder Island collecting debris and various items that fell into the sea, intending to sell them to King André. The Thin Pirate saw a pair of nice smoking boots floating, actually the remains of zombie pirate LeChuck, after his accident with the Voodoo Cannonball, which he collected with a hook. As he threw the boots into the hold with the other loot, he witnessed LeChuck's manifestation as a demon-Pirate. The two pirates soon became undead, being the first of LeChuck's new Army of the Undead, and set sail for Monkey Island.

Agent 47 (also known as "The Hitman", "Asset 47", "XAO47" and "Mr. 47", or simply by his birth name, "47", as well as many aliases, the most prominent being Tobias Rieper) is the titular protagonist of the Hitman series. He is a professional hitman and was the former top agent for the International Contract Agency (ICA) until he exposed agency information to the public, ending them permanently. After exposing the ICA and destroying Providence, both 47 and his former handler, Diana, went freelance and now operate a murder-for-hire service by themselves. His genetically enhanced body and mind - combined with his extensive knowledge, rigorous training, and decades' worth of experience as a contract killer - turned him into the world's deadliest and most efficient assassin. Agent 47 was created by Dr. Ort-Meyer as the Five Fathers' 47th clone in his underground cloning laboratory, disguised under the surface appearance of a sanitarium in Romania.

Diana Penelope Burnwood is the deuteragonist of the HITMAN series, as one of the former "handlers" at the International Contract Agency (ICA). She provided Agent 47 with clients, targets, and information in this capacity. After 47 exposed the ICA to the world, she infiltrated Providence, eventually becoming the leader (known as the Constant). She then dismantled the organization, and went freelance with 47 - the pair now operates as an independent assassination service with no ties to the ICA. Since Hitman's inception, Diana has been a prominent part of every story and proved a invaluable asset to Agent 47- as well as being one of his extremely few genuine friends.

Lucas Grey (also known as the Shadow Client or Subject 6) is an assassin who leads his own Private Militia in a war against Providence. He is the one of the two tritagonists (alongside Carlton Smith) of the Hitman series, the tritagonist of the World of Assassination trilogy, being the main antagonist of , the false main antagonist turned tritagonist of , and one of the two tritagonists of . He is the childhood friend of Agent 47, and is later revealed to be Subject 6, another of Dr. Ort-Meyer's subjects first mentioned back in Hitman: Enemy Within as a childhood bully of 47, and then later in Agent 47: Birth of the Hitman. He successfully managed to escape the Institute for Human Betterment where he, 47, and other subjects were being held, at the cost of 47 being captured and having his mind wiped.
The Constant (Arthur Edwards) and his status is a primary objective and is a VIP in The Ark Society mission in HITMAN™ 2.

Carl Ingram, also known as the Kingmaker was the patriarch of the Ingram Family, and one of the Partners of Providence. He is one of the three overarching antagonists of the Hitman series & World of Assassination trilogy, being one of the three overarching antagonists in HITMAN™ 2 and one of the three secondary antagonists in HITMAN™ III. He is one of the two targets in the HITMAN™ III mission On Top of the World.

Marcus Stuyvesant, also known as the Patron, was the patriarch of the Stuyvesant Family and one of the Partners of Providence. He is one of the three overarching antagonists of the Hitman franchise & World of Assassination trilogy, being one of the three overarching antagonists in HITMAN™ 2 and one of the three secondary antagonists in HITMAN™ III. He is one of the targets in the HITMAN™ III mission On Top of the World.

Otto Wolfgang Ort-Meyer (also known as "Dr. Ort-Meyer" or "Prof. Ort-Meyer", and occasionally spelled as Ortmeier) is one of Agent 47's five genetic fathers, and the one responsible for his creation. He is the main antagonist of , and was posthumously revealed as an operative of Providence.

Olivia Hall is the tertiary antagonist of , the false secondary antagonist of , and one of the two tritagonists of . She is a young female hacker and Lucas Grey's closest ally in the Private Militia's war against Providence.
Sierra Knox, (also known as "The Daredevil") is a target that appears in The Finish Line mission in .

Sophia Washington (also known as "the Schemer") is a target in The Ark Society mission in .
Robert Knox (also known as The Inventor) is the CEO of Kronstadt Industries. He appears as one of Agent 47's targets and minor antagonist in the mission The Finish Line.

Alma Reynard (also known as The Mastermind) is an anti-establishment freelance assassin working as one of the Shadow Client's militia's top lieutenants. She appears as the target of the mission Nightcall.

Derrick Powell, codename Stone, is an ICA sniper and a playable character in the Hitman series. In HITMAN™ 2: Sniper Assassin, he works with fellow sniper Knight in the co-op missions. He's a protagonist in the mobile phone app Hitman: The Shadows as part of the ICA sniper team "The Shadows".
Rico Delgado (also known as The Boss) is a target that appears major antagonist in the Three-Headed Serpent mission in .
Dawood Rangan (also known as "The Showman") is a target that appears in the Chasing a Ghost mission in .
Vanya Shah (also known as "The Queen"). is a target that appears in the Chasing a Ghost mission in .
Finding the Maelstrom is the main objective of identifying Wazir Kale around the slums of Mumbai in the Chasing A Ghost mission in HITMAN™ 2.
Andrea Martínez (also known as The Face) is a minor character in the mission The Showstopper. She later appears as one of Agent 47's targets in the mission Three-Headed Serpent.

She is also the one who gave Oliver the doll that would reveal himself as Drippy. Her soulmate in the Other World is the Great Sage Alicia (アリシア様 Alicia-sama).

She is a young human girl who is not scared of any monsters except occasionally Randall, who happened to be her monster. and frequently Mr. Waternoose too when working with Randall, and temporarily afraid of Sulley's roar. Boo eventually ventures through her closet to enter the monster world, where she develops a bond with Sulley and Mike.

personnages.description: Daigo Dojima (, Dōjima Daigo) is a recurring major character in the Like a Dragon series introduced in Yakuza 2. He is featured as a supporting character in Yakuza 2/Yakuza Kiwami 2, Yakuza 3/Yakuza Kiwami 3, Dark Ties, Yakuza 5, Yakuza 6, Yakuza: Like a Dragon, Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name, and Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth. He is also featured as an antagonist in Yakuza 4. In Ryu Ga Gotoku Online, he is the protagonist of the story Daigo Dojima: At the Time of Adversity. In Yakuza 0, he makes a minor appearance in a substory as a preteen boy. Once a lowly street thug, Daigo becomes the sixth chairman of the Tojo Clan by Kazuma Kiryu's recommendation, representing a new generation of the yakuza.

Makoto Date (, Date Makoto), is a recurring character in the Yakuza series first featured in the original Yakuza. He is a police detective with the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department, and one of Kazuma Kiryu's longest-running supporters.

Junichi Sudo (, Sudō Jun'ichi) is a recurring character in the Yakuza series introduced in the original Yakuza. He is the Chief of the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department's Criminal Investigations Division.
Sophia Baker is a character featured in Murdered: Soul Suspect. She is a shy ghost that has lost the ability to speak, who guides Ronan O'Connor to the Investigations of the Lake and the Shoreline.
personnages.jeux_phares: Murdered: Soul Suspect (2014) · The Shapeshifting Detective (2018)

personnages.description: Stella "The Sudarshana Gravity Well" is one of the elite Falcons serving Sumeragi Institute and one of the antagonists of Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX, appearing as the boss of the mission Sumeragi Building 13. Defeating her grants the EX Weapon Orbital Edge. The young, confident president of a powerful manufacturing company, Stella ended up serving as one of Sumeragi's Falcons to protect her android assistant Dystnine, the only one to whom she'll open up. She is an Adept possessing the Septima Gravity, which allows her to alter the gravity of her surroundings.

personnages.description: Quentin Beck (of Earth-616), also known as Mysterio, is an adversary of Spider-Man and professional illusionist.
Senior Chief Petty Officer "Voodoo" is an American sailor, Navy SEAL, and Tier 1 operator with AFO Neptune. He is a central character for Medal of Honor: Warfighter.
"Vegas" is a Tier 1 Operator and part of Delta Force. He is part of AFO Wolfpack.

Gunfighter.png Gunfighter 06 is the callsign of an AH-64 Apache in Medal of Honor (2010). The gunner is Cpt. Brad Hawkins. They also seem to offer intelligence to Bulldog 6 to relay back to Python 1 during the game's multiplayer aspect.

Reaper 3-1 is the callsign of an AC-130 gunship. It provide some danger-close fire support for AFO team Neptune, and then provide fire support for Neptune afterwards to destroy an AQ camp. The pilot is voiced by Stefan Marks. Reaper 3-1 makes its main appearance during Dorothy's a Bitch, providing over watch for Neptune and then turning the tide for the Task Force. Then it is attacked by the Taliban forces with anti-air fire, and RPG-7 rockets. They also provide overwatch during the later levels, but don't actually make an appearance.

Detective Ronan O'Connor is the protagonist of Murdered: Soul Suspect. He is shot to death while attempting to stop the Bell Killer at the beginning of the game. Using his newfound supernatural abilities, Ronan is free to explore the town of Salem, Massachusetts, from his shadowy afterlife known as Dusk. Unable to communicate with the detectives on his case, Ronan must read the minds of the living, influencing their thoughts and actions. As part of his investigation, he must interrogate the ghosts of Salem's past citizens to piece together the puzzle, while battling demonic spirits to save his soul and uncover the shocking truth about who is responsible for his death.

Joy Foster is a character and primary ally in Murdered: Soul Suspect. She is the teenage daughter of Cassandra, a medium with the ability to communicate with those who are stuck in Dusk and who works as a profiler for the Salem Police Department. Joy has seemingly inherited her mother's powers, which she utilizes in order to help Detective Ronan O'Connor solve his own murder case.

Abigail Williams, initially known as the Ghost Girl, is a main character and the primary antagonist of Murdered: Soul Suspect. She is a young ghost girl found in Dusk who watches Ronan O'Connor as he tries to solve the Bell Killer's case.
Julia O'Connor (née Reyes) is a secondary character in Murdered: Soul Suspect. She is the deceased wife of Ronan O'Connor.

Iris Campbell is a character featured in Murdered: Soul Suspect. She first appears when Ronan O'Connor and Joy Foster go to the mental asylum to find her. Iris and her twin sister, Rose, are both Mediums who are targeted by the Bell Killer for supposedly having a Contract with Demons, like Mediums of the Puritan era during the Salem Witch Trials were.

is one of the citizens in Vampyr. She works at the Turquoise Turtle. She is young and very fond of her boss Tom Watts. He describes her as angry and doesn't give their relationship much of a chance. * When Jonathan asks her about William Bishop she is clearly shocked about the man's appearance. She mentions his terrible skin and wonders if he might be contagious. * This reveals also a hint for Tom, who didn't want to answer the first time around when Jonathan approached him. * Her father was a sailor from Bombay and her mother was from Glasgow.

(Bridget Eleanor Wellington) is one of the characters in Vampyr. She is the leader of the sewer Skals. Her realm can be entered through the Night Asylum. Her introduction is in Chapter 3: Family History during the quest Give a Dog a Bad Name where she gives blood to an injured Skal who survived the attack from Fergal Bansha * Survives Harriet Jones' massacre of the Sewer Skals as she was not there at the time. * In 1738 she was turned into an immortal by her husband, who wanted to preserve her beauty. * Her husband was Lord Redgrave, who then rejected her.

Pippa is a character in Vampyr. She's working as a nurse at the Pembroke Hospital. She has a secret relationship with Milton Hooks. This could cost both of them their jobs. Jonathan E. Reid can ask her directly about this if he found out more. * If Milton Hooks dies and the player sleeps, Pippa joins the Priwen Guards and can be encountered as an enemy on the streets.
is a character in Vampyr. She is a mute florist and working for Dorothy Crane.

is one of the characters in Vampyr. She can be found in The Docks near the Turquoise Turtle Pub. She also sometimes can be watched talking to Booth Digby. She is the leader of the Wet Boot Boys. Clay Cox was her husband.

Geoffrey McCullum is the current leader of the Guard of Priwen and one of the main antagonists in Vampyr. Driven by the hatred towards vampires, McCullum and the rest of The Guard of Priwen are sworn to eradicate the immortals that occupy the city of London and most of England. Strongly believes the epidemic was intentionally created and suspects the protagonist, Jonathan Reid, to be involved.

Hitomi (Japanese: ヒトミ) is a young student and karateka, who debuted in Dead or Alive 3, replacing Ein as the regular karate martial artist in the character roster. Hitomi has been practicing the art of karate under her father's tutelage since she was a child, and enters the Dead or Alive Tournaments either to prove her skills or to see Hayate. Either reason, she is determined to win the tournament.

personnages.description: Reaver is an ex-pirate turned industry tycoon and the Hero of Skill.

Page is a character in Fable III. She is one of the active followers of the Hero of Brightwall. Page is the leader of the Bowerstone Resistance, an underground organization working against King Logan. Page and the rest of the resistance live in the privacy of the Bowerstone sewers. Page puts her resistance duties above all else, having witnessed first hand the injustice and suffering that Logan has imposed on the common folk. Though Page is never quick to trust a stranger, she is still compassionate and cares for her people.
Sir Walter Beck is a retired soldier who served as advisor and mentor to The Hero of Brightwall during the Age of Industry.

Elliot is the childhood sweetheart of the female Hero of Brightwall and is the supporting character of the quest Life in the Castle. Introduced early on, he is the one who teaches the player how to use the touch mechanic. He was first revealed at Gamescom. [http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YL60aJgICVc] There is a female character called Elise who has the same role as Elliot if the player chooses a male hero at the start of the game.

Sabine is the King of Mistpeak, and is a character in Fable III. The King of the Dwellers, Sabine developed a deep hatred for the tyrannical King Logan after he forced the Dwellers to live in the harshest and coldest reaches of the Mistpeak Mountains. Desperately trying to keep his starving people alive, the Dweller King suddenly comes face-to-face with the Hero of Brightwall, who escaped from Bowerstone Castle along with Walter using a Cullis Gate. Although the Hero wants Sabine to join in their revolution, the old Dweller is initially untrusting of the Hero, and requires the them to complete several tasks before he will agree to help in the uprising against King Logan. Sabine asks the Hero to complete three tasks for him. First, the Hero must retrieve an ancient relic (the famous Music Box of Fable II) from a dungeon beneath the Brightwall Academy to prove their worth as a Hero. Second, he asks that the Hero slay the mercenaries of Mistpeak Valley, who have been preying upon their meager food stores. Finally, he wants the Hero to convince the nearby town of Brightwall to share its food with the Dwellers. Once these tasks have been completed, upon the Hero's triumphant return to the Dweller camp, the surprised Sabine asks one final boon of the Hero-to return Mistpeak to it's former glory and give it back to the Dwellers. Once the Hero agrees, Sabine eagerly commits his people to the revolution, helping clear a path to Bowerstone Castle during the Battle for Albion. Once the

Captain Benjamin "Ben" Finn is a soldier in the Swift Brigade of the Albion Royal Army under the command of Major Swift, and an ally to the Hero of Brightwall in Fable III. He has a very strong connection with Major Swift, who is much like a father figure to Ben. As a member of the "Old Guard" and due to his connections to Major Swift, he is marked as a traitor by King Logan.

Captain Saker, or just Saker, is a character featured in Fable III and is the leader of a group of mercenaries who inhabit a camp near Brightwall located in Mistpeak. Sir Walter also mentions that Saker was a member of the army, but had more in common with bandits and cutthroats. The Hero of Brightwall must disguise as a mercenary to gain entrance to the Mercenary camp, and also purchase a beard and tattoos to appear more convincing. Once inside the base, the Hero must find Captain Saker and fight him. He surrenders, and the player is given the choice of killing him or allowing him to live. If the player decides to spare him, the Hero slaps Saker's face and then proceeds to help him stand up. He will then pledge his support and men to the revolution against Logan. Choosing this option will add Saker to the manifestations of your allies along the Road to Rule and the Mercenary Camp becomes a functional settlement, remaining populated, and allows players to purchase property and utilize services such as shops and prostitutes. Although he is accepted as a member of your rebellion, neither he nor any of his mercenaries will be present at the battle against Logan's forces. If the player decides to kill him, a short cut-scene of Saker attacking the Hero, only to be brought to the ground and executed, will be shown. Choosing this option voids all life within the camp, makes all property unusable, and does not add Saker to the Road to Rule. The camp will repopulate upon downloading U

Theresa is the blind seer of Albion and a descendant of the great archons of the Old Kingdom. She is the older sister of the legendary Hero of Oakvale. At over six hundred years old, she is among the oldest known living beings in Albion. Theresa serves as the deuteragonist in Fable, Fable: The Lost Chapters, Fable Anniversary, and Fable: The Journey. She also plays a significant supportive role in Fable II and Fable III.

is a golem character in the Soul series of fighting games. The original Astaroth made his first appearance in Soulcalibur and has returned for Soulcalibur II, Soulcalibur III, Soulcalibur Legends (as Astaroth α), Soulcalibur IV and Soulcalibur: Broken Destiny. After he is killed, a new Astaroth appears in Soulcalibur V. However, the original returned in Soulcalibur: Lost Swords and Soulcalibur: Unbreakable Soul. In the games, he is referred to as the "Black Giant". He is also given the title "魔人の尖兵" in Soulcalibur and Soulcalibur VI, which has been translated as "A Soldier of the Heretics" in the former and "Demonic Vanguard" in the latter. From Soulcalibur III to Soulcalibur Broken Destiny, his title was "", which was translated as "Destructive Executioner" in Soulcalibur Broken Destiny and "Executioner" in Soulcalibur V. In Soulcalibur V and Soulcalibur Lost Swords, his title was "滅びの運び手", or "Harbinger of Destruction" in English.

personnages.description: Oberstgruppenführer Wilhelm "Deathshead" (Totenkopf) Strasse was a leading member of the German Armed Forces, a gifted researcher and doctor who heads the SS Special Projects Division. He is the arch-nemesis of the series' protagonist William J. Blazkowicz, and the main antagonist of the Wolfenstein series. He first appears as the secondary antagonist of the 2001 Return to Castle Wolfenstein, the main antagonist of the 2009 sequel Wolfenstein, and returns as the main antagonist of the MachineGames reboot Wolfenstein: The New Order, the overarching antagonist of Wolfenstein: The Old Blood, and the posthumous antagonist of Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus.

The OSA Director is the head of the Office of Secret Actions - a military sabotage and espionage unit tasked with carrying out clandestine operations against the Nazi war effort and collaborating with allied resistance groups. B.J. Blazkowicz reports to him by sending letters after every mission is a success.
Oberstgruppenführer Viktor Zetta is the tertiary antagonist of Wolfenstein, one of four bosses in the game and one leading figure in research of the Black Sun Dimension.

Leonid Alexandrov (Russian: Леонид Александров) is the acting leader of the Golden Dawn in Wolfenstein, leading a research expedition in Isenstadt. Alexandrov led the Dawn in direct competition with the Nazis, hoping to comprehend supernatural phenomenon of the Veil before it could be used against humanity. He served as a tertiary antagonist, working to undermine B.J. Blazkowicz in favor of exploring the Black Sun, though ultimately at great consequence to himself and his aims. Alexandrov was one of B.J.'s first points of contact in Isenstadt, though he was wary of the American. Given Alexandrov's cultural and political ties to the Soviet Union, the distrust was mutual. The two were forced to work together by circumstance, however, and Alexandrov assigned B.J. several missions relating to the Golden Dawn and its objectives, including locating missing students and investigating Nazi dig sites at the local hospital. Alexandrov showed his true colors shortly thereafter, however, sacrificing one of the students B.J. had rescued by intentionally sending him to be re-captured and interrogated by the Nazi officer Richter. Once the Castle Mission is complete, he no longer appears in the Downtown area, but eventually, he is spotted again inside the Zeppelin by B.J. Blazkowicz and reveals everything. He was the mole all along and previously informed the Nazis of B.J.'s arrival at the Train Station, and possibly working with the Black Market Businessman, Anton Kriege, also providing inf
Erik Engle is the second in command of the Kreisau Circle, later becoming the leader of the resistance after Caroline's "death".

Hans Grösse (aka Hans Grosse) is a Nazi veteran. He is known for having the most 'encounters' with B.J. Blazkowicz, more than any other character in the series. *Hans Grösse (Classic) *Hans Grosse (Wolf2)
Heavy Troopers (German: Schwere Soldaten) are powerful enemies seen in Wolfenstein. They wear heavy armoured suits and carry a Particle Cannon.

personnages.description:
The character Doctor Ivo "Eggman" Robotnik is the man antagonist of the Sonic the Hedgehog franchise, created by Sega. Being a mad scientist, he constantly plans to conquer the world in order to fulfill his dream: to build his own Eggman Empire. He's the archenemy of Sonic, and wants to do everything in his power to stand as the last winner. Spme of Eggman's basic characteristics is his egg-shaped body, his sunglasses, his clothing in red, black and yellow, as well as his very large mustache.

Outside of appearing in almost every Sonic the Hedgehog video game, he's also a recurring character in other media such as comics, animations and novels.

Eggman loves machines and is often described as a genius with an IQ of 300. He doesn't care for others' opinions and never gives up on his desire to build the ultimate "utopia". Whoever interrupt his plans, becomes a prime threat and a target. Although Sonic has always ruined his evil plans, Eggman holds a secret respect for his determination.

Many of the robots in the earlier games are actually animals that Robotnik trapped in mechanical outfits. These are the same animals that Sonic frees at the end of each level.
personnages.jeux_phares: Sonic Adventure 2 (2001) · Team Sonic Racing (2019) · Sonic Boom: Rise of Lyric (2014)

personnages.description: , also formerly known as , is a character that appears in the Sonic the Hedgehog series. She is an anthropomorphic pink hedgehog with a crush on Sonic the Hedgehog. Since meeting Sonic on Little Planet, Amy has declared herself his girlfriend and has attempted to win his heart by any means in many of their adventures. She wields the Piko Piko Hammer, which she uses with skills second to none and never leaves home without. Amy is a cheerful, though slightly erratic girl, with a positive attitude and nature and boundless energy. However, she has a fiery temper and her infatuation with Sonic makes her short-sighted and a bit obsessive about him, having followed him everywhere since meeting him. Nevertheless, she has a pure heart and will not let anything stop her.

personnages.description: Jameson Locke is a SPARTAN-IV in the United Nations Space Command.
Olympia Vale (SN: 44482-91201-OV) is a human post-war political liaison affiliated with the Office of Naval Intelligence.

The Arbiter is the sixth campaign level of Halo 2, which introduces the Arbiter Thel 'Vadamee as a playable character for the first time. You must assassinate the Heretic Leader on a Forerunner Gas Mine in Threshold's atmosphere. The mission involves neutralizing Heretic forces. Along the way, the player will have to open a hangar door for reinforcements, fight, for the first time in Halo 2, Sentinels, and fly a Heretic Banshee to escort a friendly Phantom that is looking for where the Heretic Leader escaped to. This is also the first time in Halo 2 you are able to use the Covenant Carbine, the Sentinel Beam, and the Fuel Rod Gun. It is also the first time members of the Covenant aid you. Your allies are Special Operations Elites and Special Operations Grunts, meaning that you start off with rather powerful friendly units.
Sloan was a smart AI owned by the mining company Liang Dortmund, who acted as governor of the company's settlements on Meridian.

Petty Officer Second Class Kelly-087, born Kelly Shaddock, is one of the few SPARTAN-II supersoldiers. She is well-known due to close friendships with Joshua-029, Samuel-034, Linda-058, Frederic-104, and John-117. She was temporarily missing, but was later reunited with the remaining SPARTAN-IIs (excluding John-117) on Onyx. She, along with the other surviving SPARTAN-IIs and several SPARTAN-IIIs, were trapped in a Micro Dyson Sphere, but were able to exit the sphere and link up with UNSC ONI ships (, , and ). She is one of John's closest friends and is renowned for her incredible speed, even with her Mjolnir Armor. By 2558 she had engaged in 201 operations (124 campaigns).
Holly Tanaka (SN: 93312-28001-HT) is a Spartan-IV in the United Nations Space Command.

Captain Thomas J. Lasky (SN: 98604-72690-TL) is a human senior naval officer of the UNSC Navy who served throughout the Human-Covenant war and in the post-war years. Since at least 2552, Lasky had served as Captain Del Rio's executive officer aboard . Following Del Rio's removal from command by FLEETCOM after abandoning John-117 on Requiem, Lasky was named acting captain of Infinity and aided John-117 in his battle against the Didact. Six months after the Didact's attack on Earth, Lasky, now Captain, led Infinity in the assault on Requiem as per FLEETCOM's orders. Throughout the campaign in and around Requiem Lasky showed the true potential he held in command, especially in terms of keeping morale high as well as defending his men when Infinity was invaded by Promethean Knights. Also when requesting the help of Catherine Halsey, the Office of Naval Intelligence allowed it, as Lasky had shown his commitment to the UNSC in terms of following every order given, to the extent of keeping John-117's re-emergence secret from Dr. Halsey. He is the main protagonist of Halo 4: Forward Unto Dawn.

Catherine Elizabeth Halsey, MD, PhD (SN: CC-409871), was a praised scientist and former employee turned prisoner of the Office of Naval Intelligence, best known as the creator of the SPARTAN-II Program and Mjolnir Powered Assault Armor. Despite being a civilian, she held considerable authority within ONI and commanded considerable respect from many military figures. As she grew older, Halsey took various extreme measures to protect her remaining Spartans, even going against the military law to do so - a choice which would result in her eventual arrest by ONI's Kilo-Five in 2553. In 2558 when Admiral Osman ordered Catherine's execution, Catherine escaped the assassination attempt and defected to Jul 'Mdama's Covenant.

Lieutenant, Junior Grade Frederic-104, born Frederic Ellsworth, is a Spartan-II Commando and is one of the few surviving SPARTAN-IIs. Historically, Frederic-104 has held the highest rank among any of the active SPARTAN-IIs except for Kurt-051. He has been known to become greatly affected by his injured teammates. He has also had a close working relationship with John-117. During the final three months of the Human-Covenant war, Fred was active in the Forerunner shield world installation at the core of the former planet Onyx. He was retrieved by Kilo-Five in February 2553, along with fellow Spartans Kelly-087 and Linda-058 and the SPARTAN-III Petty Officers Tom, Lucy and Team Saber.

Captain James Dominic Fenix, (COG Tags CSID: 257412-W67M1-VQ) also known as JD Fenix, was a Gear officer in the Coalition of Ordered Governments Army currently serving in the Swarm Invasion. Son of war hero Marcus Fenix and First Minister Anya Stroud, Fenix was one of the first humans to be born from the fertility program created by the Ministry of Procreation of the reformed Coalition of Ordered Governments following the Locust War. The very same fertility program later caused Stroud's death when she attempted to conceive a second child. Fenix continued his education and enrolled in the COG Army military academy, along with childhood friend Delmont Walker. The two graduated in 39 A.E. and enlisted in the COG Army as lieutenants. During the Interwar Period, Fenix and Walker were in command of combat DeeBees and stationed in Settlement 2. Political unrest grew in the settlement due to lack of autonomy under New Ephyra and First Minister Mina Jinn's rule. During a protest in 41 A.E. that grew into a riot, Fenix was ordered by Jinn to command the DeeBees into opening fire on the protestors. The massacre affected Walker, causing him to go AWOL. Fenix joined him out of friendship and became Outsiders, participating in the Outsider Movement. They later joined the Outsider village of Fort Umson, led by Chief Reyna Diaz. Fenix and Walker soon after befriended Reyna's daughter, Kait Diaz. Fenix and Walker assisted Fort Umson in raiding COG installations and Settlements for supplies. O

Kait Diaz is a Coalition of Ordered Governments Army corporal currently serving in the Swarm Invasion. Daughter of war hero Gabriel Diaz and civilian Reyna Torres as well as being the granddaughter of Queen Myrrah. Gabriel and Reyna became the first Outsiders following the end of the Locust War by establishing Fort Umson. They began the Outsider Movement in protest of the reformed Coalition of Ordered Governments by living outside COG jurisdiction and in the Wilds. Both her parents were fugitives of the state during the war and had distrust for the COG. From her parents, and later her uncle Oscar Diaz after Gabriel's death, Kait received extensive training in survival and combat. In 41 A.E., Kait met and befriended newcomers James Dominic Fenix and Delmont Walker. In 42 A.E., an evolved species of the Locust called the Swarm ambushed Fort Umson. Except for Kait, JD, Del, and Oscar; all the villagers, including Reyna, were taken. While trying to rescue their people, Kait's group discovered the the villagers were transformed into Drones for Swarm while Reyna was integrated within a Hive to become their new Queen. Upon her mother's request, Kait disconnected and euthanized Reyna. The Swarm's Hivemind began to contact Kait. After remotely controlling a Warden to kill her uncle, Kait went on a mission to uncover her family's origins and prevent her from becoming the Swarm's Queen. Kait discovered her grandmother was Myrrah, whose consciousness was still alive within the Hivemind.

Chief Oscar Diaz (COG Tags CSID: 395274-T2V26-LP) ES was a former Gear Sergeant in the Pendulum Wars and Locust War, and an Outsider in the Outsider Movement. He was the brother of Lt. Colonel Gabriel Diaz, adoptive brother to Wyatt Callahan, the brother-in-law to Reyna Diaz, and the uncle to Kait Diaz. Following the end of the Locust War, he and his brothers became Outsiders and built their own Outsider Village, with Lt. Colonel Diaz leading. After his brother's death, Reyna became the leader of the Diaz Village, with Oscar continuing to help lead with her. After the village's destruction, he became the leader of Riftworm Village.

Reyna Diaz (née Torres; c. 30 B.E. - Bloom 42 A.E.), also known as Subject TE-872-3, is Queen of the Swarm. Born to Queen Myrrah and Doctor Torres, she was the subject of experiments at Mount Kadar Laboratory by Doctor Niles Samson due to her shared genetic traits with her mother, who was also a subject. The experiments involved the creation of the Locust and Myrrah's control over them through the Hivemind. Torres fled the facility with Reyna to protect her from Samson's experiments. In the years prior to Emergence Day, Torres and Reyna avoided COG jurisdiction due to his indictment for his involvement at the New Hope Research Facility. In 1 A.E., Reyna and Torres took shelter at Zenic Laboratory in Vasgar before it was sieged by Locust scientist Ukkon. Torres was killed and Reyna was imprisoned. She was later liberated by Sergeant Gabriel Diaz of the COG Army and killed Ukkon. Gabriel later abandoned the COG and became Stranded along with Reyna and formed the Outsiders during the reformation of the COG following the end of the Locust War, with Reyna acting as Chief of Fort Umson. Reyna and Gabriel eventually married and had a daughter, Kait. Gabriel later died from Rustlung, resulting in his brother Oscar supporting Reyna and Kait. In 42 A.E., the Locust evolved into the Swarm. Lacking their queen due to Myrrah's death, the Swarm located Reyna and ambushed the village in order to connect her to the Swarm Hive, allowing Myrrah's consciousness to use her body in leading the Sw
Richard Dalmore was a reporter that worked for the Coalition News Channel.

Sergeant Bernadette "Bernie" Mataki, SM, affectionately known as Boomer Lady by Augustus Cole and Granny by Damon Baird, is a Gear in the Coalition of Ordered Governments armed forces. Bernie was born on the island of Galangi in the South Islands during the 33rd year of the Pendulum Wars. She is the daughter of a farmer, who came from a Northerner family, and the sister of Michael Mataki. After joining the COG at eighteen years of age, she became one of the best snipers in the army. She spent most of her career in the 26th Royal Tyran infantry, serving in several different companies. She fought in several of the most important battles of the Pendulum Wars, including the Battle of Shavad and Aspho Fields. After Emergence Day, she was stranded on her home island until she heard about the recall to Ephyra, and decided to go on a several year trek across the world to rejoin the COG, eventually reaching the Jacinto Plateau. She reunited with her oldest friend Colonel Victor Hoffman, restarting a relationship with him, and served in Delta-One briefly after the Lightmass Offensive and again after Operation: Hollow Storm, as well as during the Stranded Insurgency and the beginning of the Lambent Pandemic. When the COG collapsed, Bernie traveled with Hoffman, several hundred Gears, and thousands of civilians to Anvil Gate. Bernie and Hoffman successfully defended Anvil Gate from Locust and Lambent forces. The Imulsion countermeasure neutralized both species, ending the Locust War. Ber

Loki is the child-like supernatural being whom is the good personality of the first incarnation the former God of Chaos, Lord Aesir. Split shortly after the creation of the Eyes of the World, he later finds himself in the present time with amnesia and a yearning to reach the sacred mountain of Fimbulventr and later meets Bayonetta. He allies himself with the witch when their quest converges on going to the sacred mountain by striking a deal with Bayonetta to get the two of them through, claiming that his mysterious powers will prove necessary to reach the Gates of Hell and save Jeanne's soul. Loki is a major supporting character of Bayonetta 2 and is even briefly playable during the event of the game.

personnages.description: Orkos (Greek: Όρκους) is a Fury and the deuteragonist in God of War: Ascension. He is a half-God and half-Fury, son of Ares and Alecto.
Aletheia (Greek: ἀλήθεια) was the Oracle of Delphi who helped Kratos in his quest to free himself from his blood oath to Ares and defeat the Furies who bound him to the insane war god.

The Spartans were the ancient Greek warrior people of the city state of Sparta, whose army were the main personification of all things Spartan in the God of War universe, were an important part in military history.

Castor (Greek: Κάστωρ) and Pollux (Greek: Πολυδεύκης), also known as the Dioscuri and as the Gemini Twins, were Greek mortal (Castor) and Demigod (Pollux) twins, with Pollux being the son of Zeus and half-brother to Kratos. They appear as bosses in God of War: Ascension.

Lysandra (Greek: Λυσάνδρα) was a Spartan woman who was Kratos' first wife and mother to his daughter, Calliope. Though Kratos had many women in his time, he felt truly connected to Lysandra and considered her his soul mate and true love. Lysandra was also the only person who did not fear Kratos during his time as a brutal Spartan captain, and, on more than one occasion, questioned his reasons for the reckless slaughter of many innocent people.
Archimedes is a minor character that appears in God of War: Ascension.
The Training Soldier is a character that appears exclusively in the Multiplayer of God of War: Ascension. As his name implies, he is the warrior who trains new players for the game.

is one of the main protagonists of Namco's Soul series of fighting games. First appearing in Soulcalibur, he has returned as a starting character for all subsequent games in the series, with the exception of Soulcalibur Legends and Soulcalibur: Lost Swords. Kilik is well known among Soulcalibur fans for his defining practice of rod martial arts. Kilik returns in Soulcalibur V as a mimic character who uses at random the fighting styles used by male characters, as opposed to Elysium, who mimics female styles and Edge Master, who mimics all styles. One method of unlocking him is to defeat him in Arcade mode (setting on Asia route). Another method is by defeating him in the first stage of Legendary Souls mode with any playable character. In Soulcalibur and Soulcalibur VI, his title is "目覚めし宿命", which was translated as "Destiny Awakened" in both games whilst in Legend of SOULCALIBUR, it was translated as "Awaken destiny". The title that he had from Soulcalibur III to Soulcalibur: Broken Destiny was "の" (Guren no Jouka), which was translated as "Sacred Fire of the Red Lotus" in Soulcalibur Broken Destiny, and "Red Lotus" in Soulcalibur V and Soulcalibur VI. His title in Soulcalibur V is "かつて宿命を背負いし者". What lies in his soul is Valor.

Maxi (マキシ, Makishi, also written as 真喜志) is a character in the Soul series of fighting games. He made his first appearance in Soulcalibur and returned in Soulcalibur II, Soulcalibur III, Soulcalibur IV, Soulcalibur: Broken Destiny, Soulcalibur V, Soulcalibur: Unbreakable Soul, Soulcalibur: Lost Swords and Soulcalibur VI.
is a character in the Soul series of fighting games. He is a mainstay of the series and one of most iconic characters in the franchise.

Yoshimitsu (吉光) is the name given to the wielder of the Yoshimitsu sword and leader of the Manji Clan. So far in the series, there have been two Yoshimitsus: the first and the second, with the latter only appearing in Soulcalibur V. Each Yoshimitsu has the same fighting style, weaponry, and voice. They also all have a similar appearance. This is so that to outsiders of the Manji Clan, it appears as though there is only one immortal Yoshimitsu. The first Yoshimitsu's title in Soulcalibur and Soulcalibur VI is 元祖からくり忍, which has been translated into English as "The First Mechanized Ninja" in Soulcalibur, and "The Original Mechanical Ninja" in Soulcalibur VI. From Soulcalibur III to Soulcalibur: Broken Destiny, his title would be changed to 初代卍党首領 (later written as 初代万字党首領), which would be translated as "First Manji Clan Leader" in Soulcalibur Broken Destiny, and "First Manji Leader" in Soulcalibur VI. Yoshimitsu the Second's title in Soulcalibur V is He who lives by the code (仁義に生きる男).

is one of the most central characters of the Soul series and the main protagonist in most of its installments. He is a mainstay of the Soulcalibur series and one of the most iconic characters in the franchise.

The is a character in the Soul series of fighting games. Edge Master made his first playable appearance in Soulcalibur, but still makes actions in the background throughout most of the series. He returns as a playable boss character in Soulcalibur V. His title in Soulcalibur and Soulcalibur V is "刃を極めし者". This would be translated as "The Master of Blades" in the English Dreamcast port of Soulcalibur, and as "Katana Master" in Soulcalibur Broken Destiny and Soulcalibur V. What lies in his soul is: Experience In Soulcalibur V's promotional material he is referred to as True Master of the Edge.

Dan was a member of Wardenclyffe Section's Charon Corps, a unit belonging to a secret research organization of the United States government that was dedicated to the investigation of several mysterious infectious organisms, acting as the combat engineer for the group.
personnages.jeux_phares: Bully: Scholarship Edition (2008) · Metal Gear Survive (2018)

personnages.description: James "Mac" MacAllan was a former officer of the IMC Colonial Navy, serving as Executive Officer (XO) on IMS Odyssey under the command of Vice Admiral (and friend) Marcus Graves, before his mutiny at the end of the Titan Wars. Eventually, he would join the Frontier Militia, becoming the commander of the 1st Militia Fleet and would eventually lead the Marauder Corps in the Battle of Demeter, where he would ultimately sacrifice himself and his forces to ensure Militia victory against IMC forces.

In the IMC command structure, Vice Admiral Marcus Graves is formally known as the Cincfront, or Commander-in-Chief, Frontier Command. He serves as a supporting character for the IMC Campaign of Titanfall.
Cheng "Bish" Lorck is a Combat Intelligence Specialist who operates for the Frontier Militia. He is a major supporting character for the Militia campaign in Titanfall.

Kuben Blisk is a South African mercenary Pilot who served in the IMC's forces as a ranking commander and contracted mercenary. He is the leader of the Apex Predators, an infamous outfit of ruthless freelance Pilots. After the end of the Frontier War, he went on to create a popular bloodsport competition called the Apex Games. He serves as the deuteragonist in the IMC story in Titanfall, the secondary antagonist of Titanfall 2, and plays a background role in Apex Legends.

Spyglass is a physical manifestation for the IMC's vast computational network identity. He serves as a supporting character in the IMC campaign in Titanfall and handles Titan deployment for the IMC forces.

One of the major interplanetary corporations that exist within the universe of Titanfall, Hammond Robotics is a major manufacturing, aerospace and defense contractor allied with the IMC. Claiming to have been at the forefront of robot design since the 20th century, Hammond produces considerable amounts of war material for the IMC cause, including Titans, Marvins and Spectres. Their logo can be found on all Titan briefing videos. The company is also involved in the Simulacrum and energy fields.
Lotti, formerly known as Lotto, is a character in the Deponia series.
Lonzo is a character in the Deponia series. He is the owner of the local Kuvaq bar.
Argus is an antagonist in the Deponia series. He is the bailiff of the Organon army.
Wenzel is a character in the Deponia series

"Challenge me when you are ready to duel a god." ---- Justice (ジャスティス, Jasutisu) is the main antagonist of the Afro Samurai anime and manga series. He is an enigmatic and power-hungry gunslinger seeking the headbands to become the only unstoppable force and the arch-nemesis of the titular protagonist, Afro, directly being the killer of the latter's father. He was the holder of the Number One Headband for most of the first anime.

personnages.description: Mr. Oswald Mandus is the main character of Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs. He was a wealthy industrialist and passionate inventor who took out massive loans to try to apply his new machinery to his businesses; however, he was unable to make a turn in profit. In his desperation, Mandus went through the journals of his great-uncle, which was the catalyst for the events of the game. Everything mechanical in his estate seems to be of his own design. Mandus is voiced by English voice actor Toby Longworth.

The Machine is the main antagonist of . It was a sprawling network of tunnels and factories situated underneath Victorian London, created by Oswald Mandus, and it gained sentience after part of his soul was inserted. The Machine's malevolent sentience was also referred to euphemistically as "the Engineer" in Mandus's conversation with the Professor. The conscious Machine was the wicked half of Oswald Mandus’ soul, torn apart from his body and given independent existence in the Orb he recovered, which was integrated into the machinery. It controlled both the slaughtering of humans and was partially responsible for the creation of the Manpigs.

Edwin Mandus and Enoch Mandus are the sons of Oswald and Lily Mandus. The boys are twins, more likely identical than fraternal. Edwin was born before Enoch. It is unknown if the children seen in game are their ghosts or simply hallucinations, as they were killed over 10 months before the events of the game.

Lucifer, also known as Satan and The Devil, is the overarching antagonist of 2008's Alone in the Dark. A fallen angel, Lucifer was stripped of his station in Heaven after leading a failed coup against God. As punishment, his throne was shattered and Lucifer's soul was ripped out and cast down to Earth to live as a man. Embittered and driven mad by his mortality, Lucifer collected the pieces of his throne and summoned forth all of his anger and remaining powers; creating the Philosopher's Stone both to anchor his influence into the living world as well as to corrupt its Carriers into his slaves. Using the Stone's powers, particularly its promise of eternal life and kingly fortunes, Lucifer influenced great men over the course of history; transforming each into his slave. Under his control, they built a temple beneath Central Park to serve as a gateway to the netherworld. However, his plans were stalled when the alchemist Hermes Treismajice discovered his deception and stole the Stone, breaking it into two halves; one he kept for protection, the other he sent out into the world where it drifted from Carrier to Carrier throughout several centuries. Eventually, Lucifer found himself in the body of Edward Carnby, a paranormal private investigator who became the Carrier of the free half of the Stone in the 1920's. During the possession, Lucifer became so accustomed to Edward that he became his perfect vessel; the True Carrier.

personnages.description: Ethan Seed is the secondary antagonist in Far Cry New Dawn. He is the son of Joseph Seed and the leader of New Eden after Joseph decided to head north.
Louise, who is frequently referred to as Lou, is the twin sister of Mickey and one of the two main antagonists of Far Cry New Dawn.

Joseph Seed, also known as "The Father", is the main antagonist of Far Cry 5, Inside Eden's Gate and the deuteragonist of Far Cry New Dawn. He is a ruthless megalomaniac who is the founder and the leader of the Hope County-based extremist religious terrorist cult organization "Project at Eden's Gate" alongside his brothers and adoptive sister who he dubs "The Heralds"; Jacob, John, and Faith Seed. Eden's Gate has used both coercion and violence to bring the existing residents of Hope County into its cult, as ordered by Seed, and, as of the events depicted in the game, is in direct conflict with The Resistance and its members. After the nuclear apocalypse, he created a successor religious organization, The New Eden.
Carmina Rye is a supporting character in Far Cry 5 and a main character in Far Cry New Dawn. She is the daughter of Nick and Kim Rye.

Kimiko Rye, known primarily as Kim, is a character in Far Cry 5 and Far Cry New Dawn. She is the wife of Nick Rye, and the mother of Carmina Rye. Kim’s parents (and possibly Kim herself) are from Canada and heavily disapproved of her marriage to Nick and choice to live in Montana, only staying six hours for the wedding. Nick states that even before the cult they found Hope County to be a dangerous place full of guns.

Thousands of years later, she aids the Prince when his brother, Malik, releases the army and Ratash. She acts as one of the protagonists in Prince of Persia: The Forgotten Sands.
